title: Apple Announces Mac Studio Pricing: 512 GB RAM Model Hits Market at Premium Price
body:
Apple has finally disclosed the price tag for the most powerful Mac Studio configuration yet—a model equipped with a staggering 512 GB of unified memory. The high‑end machine, which pairs the new M5 Ultra chip with the massive RAM capacity, will be available for purchase starting in October at a list price of $19,999. The announcement confirms the spec that Apple hinted at during the August launch of the M5 Max and M5 Ultra variants, and it signals the company’s continued push to position the Mac Studio as the go‑to workstation for demanding creative and scientific workloads.

The 512 GB Mac Studio is built around the M5 Ultra, Apple’s most advanced silicon to date. The chip combines two M5 Max dies using a high‑bandwidth interconnect, delivering up to 64 CPU cores, 128 GPU cores, and a dedicated 64‑core Neural Engine. With the expanded unified memory pool, the system can keep massive datasets—such as 8K video timelines, complex 3D scenes, or large‑scale machine‑learning models—resident in fast, low‑latency RAM, eliminating the need for external storage swaps that can bottleneck performance. Apple claims the configuration can sustain up to 2 TB/s memory bandwidth, a figure that dwarfs the capabilities of most competing desktop platforms.

Pricing for the 512 GB variant places it firmly in the realm of enterprise‑grade hardware. At $19,999, the Mac Studio sits above the top‑end offerings from traditional PC workstations that rely on Intel or AMD CPUs paired with discrete GPUs. However, Apple argues that the integrated architecture—where CPU, GPU, and Neural Engine share the same memory pool—delivers efficiency gains that translate into lower power consumption and quieter operation. The compact 7.7‑inch square chassis, which can be mounted on a desk or rack, also offers a smaller footprint than many of its rivals, a factor that could appeal to studios and labs where space is at a premium.

Industry analysts see the move as Apple’s attempt to capture a niche yet lucrative segment of the professional market that has traditionally gravitated toward Windows‑based workstations. The company’s earlier forays into high‑performance desktop hardware, such as the Mac Pro, struggled to gain traction due to limited configurability and a steep price curve. By offering a pre‑configured, ultra‑powerful system with a fixed price, Apple sidesteps the complexity of custom builds while still delivering performance that rivals or exceeds many custom‑assembled rigs. The 512 GB option also underscores Apple’s confidence that a growing number of creators—film editors, visual effects artists, and AI researchers—are willing to invest in premium hardware to accelerate their workflows.

The new Mac Studio arrives at a time when the demand for on‑premises compute power is resurging. While cloud services continue to dominate many sectors, latency‑sensitive tasks such as real‑time rendering, live‑event video processing, and edge AI inference still benefit from local hardware. Apple’s expanded memory offering could therefore attract enterprises looking to keep critical workloads in‑house while leveraging the efficiency of Apple silicon. Moreover, the Mac Studio’s compatibility with macOS’s suite of professional applications—Final Cut Pro, Logic Pro, and the upcoming updates to the Apple Vision framework—means that software developers will have a powerful target platform for optimizing next‑generation tools.

Looking ahead, the 512 GB Mac Studio may set a new benchmark for what is considered feasible in a compact desktop form factor. As Apple continues to refine its silicon roadmap, we can expect even higher core counts and memory capacities in future iterations, potentially narrowing the gap between consumer‑grade and enterprise‑grade performance. For now, the announcement reaffirms Apple’s commitment to serving the most demanding users, and it will be interesting to see how quickly professionals adopt the new configuration in a market that values both raw power and the seamless ecosystem that Apple provides.
